A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FreqPolicy study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulation results, ablations, frequency analyses and physical robotic handover experiments, including an original RoboCasa result in Appendix F.1.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds experiments using low-quality and Gaussian-corrupted demonstrations.

M1.justification: The frequency hierarchy, masked encoder-decoder, continuous diffusion tokens, loss and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. V2 clarifies training versus inference and illustrates frequency progression. The inverse-DCT equation correction does not establish a change to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds training-data-quality scenarios using suboptimal and Gaussian-corrupted demonstrations on existing Adroit and Meta-World tasks. The benchmark and manipulation-task roster otherwise remains unchanged; RoboCasa was already evaluated in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained experiments use the same comparators. The new robustness study uses existing baselines DP3 and Mamba Policy; it introduces no new comparison method. RoboCasa's BC-Transformer, Diffusion Policy and GR00T-N1 comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New Table 5 introduces reduced-reward demonstration selection on five tasks and Gaussian corruption with standard deviations 0.025, 0.05 and 0.1 on six tasks, plus relative changes against clean results. These are additional protocols; existing training budgets, horizons and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a targeted robustness study testing sensitivity to demonstration quality and increasing Gaussian noise. Existing DCT, masking, horizon, sampling-iteration and generalization analyses remain, and the appendix frequency-analysis figures are unchanged.

E5.justification: Existing error bars and three-seed descriptions are retained. New Table 5 supplies point estimates and relative changes without additional uncertainty estimates. Its Gaussian standard deviations specify corruption levels, not statistical uncertainty; the checklist merely reiterates existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 5 adds robustness results: at noise standard deviation 0.1, reported average success is 33% for FreqPolicy, 23% for DP3 and 19% for Mamba. FreqPolicy's Hammer scores are 70%, 51% and 15% across increasing noise levels, versus zero for both baselines. Previously reported numerical results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 2 corrects the inverse transform from (X0/2 + sum)/N to (X0 + 2 sum)/N, resolving a factor-of-two error relative to Equation 1. No theorem or proof is added. Appendix F.2's energy-ratio formula explains an existing measurement.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical frequency modeling, continuous representations, accuracy and efficiency. The added robustness evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: The new robustness discussion attributes noise resistance to progressive filtering and structural constraints, and interprets some small-noise gains as beneficial augmentation. Existing limitations and VLA interpretations are retained; moving Appendix G's limitations into Section 6 adds no new limitation.

D1.justification: V2 adds project and code links, explicitly describes DCT application per action dimension, and specifies the energy-ratio calculation. Existing hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged. Actual code availability is unresolved because the added checklist says it is not yet public despite the front-page code link.

R1.justification: The same 50 research references and substantive related-work positioning are retained, including the relationships to FAST, FAR, MAR, CARP and DensePolicy. No new research comparison or novelty positioning is introduced.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the method overview, clarifies dimensions and frequency indices, and adds a worked generation example. It relocates limitations into the main text and adds acknowledgements and a checklist. Most scientific prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the noise-robustness table, revises several captions and rearranges existing tables within the main text. All 30 figures are retained; the appendix frequency-figure pages are visually identical apart from pagination. There is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical correctness through the inverse-DCT correction and adds direct evidence for noise robustness, alongside clearer method explanations. The gain is limited by errors in the new aggregate reporting: FreqPolicy's five low-quality task scores and matching Table 10 baselines imply about a 35% decline, rather than Table 5's 44%. This weakens that summary, but the task-level comparisons and equation repair still provide a modest net improvement.
